This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 07.10.2023 passed by the Special Judge S.C./S.T. Act/Additional Session Judge, Court No. 10, Kanpur Nagar.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed the present offence.

Further submitted that in this case, F.I.R. was lodged against other co-accused persons with the appellant who has committed no offence but his photograph was used by co-accused Awadhesh Srivastava and account was opened in his name.
The money was also transferred in the account of Awadesh Srivastava through RTGS by the informant and land was transferred in favour of the informant by Awadesh Srivastava and Vivek Chaudhary.
The present appellant has no concern either with the land or with the money.
The statement of the informant was also recorded by the Investigating Officer in which he also alleged that the appellant was taken by the co-accused Vivek Chaudhary and Awadhesh Srivastava.
Co-accused Vivek Chaudhary has already been granted bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 28053 of 2023 vide order dated 1.11.2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 28053 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The role of present appellant cannot be said to be different from that of co-accused.
There is no any other material on record to show the complicity of the appellant in the present case.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Appellant is in jail since 24.5.2023.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

On the other hand, learned AGA opposing the prayer for bail.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellantPremchandra Gupta involved in Case Crime No. 06 of 2023, under Sections 406,
420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(5), 3(1)Da and Dha SC/ST Act, P.S. Rawatpur,
District Kanpur Nagar be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Further,
before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
